text: 🍿 The Angry Birds Movie 3 rips off the Dune poster and somehow earns it 📆 Estreno: December 23, 2026 🎭 Género: #Animation · #Comedy · #Family ✈️ Add to watchlist "Lisan al Birdee." That poster is funnier than most blockbuster marketing this year. Director John Rice and Jason Sudeikis are leaning hard into self-awareness, and it works. The first The Angry Birds Movie had no business being as funny as it was. Solid jokes, real craft underneath the IP slop. Three films in, the franchise is still betting on meme culture as its engine, and honestly, that bet looks smarter every time.

🧠 Idiocracy turns 20. It was right about everything except the timeline. Mike Judge gave President Camacho 500 years to emerge. We're speedrunning it in real time. The film's sharpest joke isn't the Brawndo ads or the toilet humor, it's that Camacho actually listened to an expert when it counted. That's the detail that stings most in 2026. Idiocracy didn't predict collapse or dictatorship. It predicted a world that stays just functional enough to keep humiliating itself, and somehow that's the scarier outcome. ✈️ Add to watchlist

🍿 Pokémon: Wild Card is real, and the poster already hits different 📆 Estreno: 2027 🎭 Género: #Animation #Adventure ✈️ Add to watchlist Seven years since Detective Pikachu and the franchise skips live-action entirely. Director Katsuhiko Kitada and CloverWorks (of Spy x Family ) are centering a TCG player and Mimikyu. That alone is a more interesting premise than any nostalgia-bait reboot. The poster leans hard cyberpunk: dark palette, sharp angles. For a franchise that lived in pastel comfort for decades, this is a real tonal bet. Cautiously sold.
